title: Explaining GNN Explanations with Edge Gradients

problem.claim: GNN explanation methods have mixed results and often struggle with complex GNN architectures and tasks.

gap.claim: A more careful theoretical analysis of competing GNN explanation methods is needed.

contributions.claim: The work establishes theoretical connections between perturbation-based and classical gradient-based GNN explanation methods, and identifies connections among other recently proposed methods.
For input-level explanations, the work identifies conditions under which GNNExplainer can be approximated by a heuristic based on the sign of edge gradients.
For layerwise explanations, the work shows that edge gradients are equivalent to occlusion search for linear GNNs.

author_reported_evidence.claim: The authors report experiments on synthetic and real datasets showing how their theoretical results manifest in practice.

narrative_sequence.summary: The success of GNNs has led to many methods for explaining their predictions.
The state of GNN explainability is unsettled, with mixed comparisons and difficulties on complex architectures and tasks.
The work analyzes input-level explanations over input graphs and layerwise explanations over computation graphs.

It connects perturbation-based and gradient-based methods, relates GNNExplainer to signed edge-gradient heuristics under stated conditions, and equates edge gradients with occlusion search for linear GNNs.
Experiments on synthetic and real datasets illustrate the theoretical results.

source_observation.claim: The abstract reports theoretical connections between perturbation-based, gradient-based, and other GNN explanation methods.

interpretation.claim: Comparing explanation methods through shared theoretical structure may clarify mixed empirical comparisons.

application.claim: When evaluating explanation methods, analyze whether apparently different methods reduce to related mechanisms under explicit conditions.

exception.claim: The reported approximation is conditional for GNNExplainer, and the reported equivalence applies to linear GNNs.

unknowns: The abstract does not specify the conditions for the GNNExplainer approximation.
The abstract does not identify the synthetic or real datasets, architectures, metrics, or quantitative results.
The abstract does not describe the scope of the connections involving other recently proposed methods.
